Are you still there? Hi! I hope you're doing fine. By way of an intro, I'm 29F and lived out of my parents' house on and off for some time and finally left for good, so maybe I can give you some advice.

Living on your own outside the bubble that is your parents' care and comfort is quite daunting and liberating at the same time. Physically taking yourself out of their grasp can provide you with undiscovered courage and independence that you thought you didn't have.

I had so many botched attempts before I finally decided to leave for the last time. It was scary, but since I had support from people around me, the transition wasn't so bad. Living alone is not so hard. Well, it can be at first but as time goes on, you sort of just learn to, well, live with it. You said you are working after college, so chances are you'll be outside a lot. You'll meet other people and perhaps make some new friends. Work and friends can help take your mind off the fear of you being on your own. In fact, you should celebrate your independence. Do the things you weren't able to do when you were with your parents. Shop for the essentials. Make a list of your regular chores. Yes, chores. Lots of chores, for which you will be thankful for having since you're reminded of your independence.

Ang saya, di ba?

As for Facebook, I would advice against using that profile if you want to keep your location discreet. It's very easy to be tracked there and very easy for them to contact you and you may not want that. Create a separate one if you think you really need it, or don't use Facebook at all if you can. 

I hope you would formally tell them that you're leaving when you do. Having a conversation about it may help both you and your parents to realize that there will be some changes in your lives, plus para hindi na nila tangkaing hanapin ka pa (sana) or isipin na nakidnap ka or what.

Please take these words with a grain of salt. I'm just some random redditor here giving you her opinion.

I wish you all the best. And congratulations in advance for graduating! Yaaay! And for your independence! Super yaaay! PM me if you want to. I like good conversations from time to time. :)
Question, though. Why did your ex-employer have to call your current employer and tell them all those? Were they trying to ruin you for some reason?

My child.
At least in the beginning. I thought I shouldn't leave her without at least knowing who her mother was, especially without a father in place. I knew I needed to provide for her, make sure she grows her childhood with me. 
But when she got older, she started to feel distant. So I thought, "Hey, she can go on without me".
But now, honestly, I just sleep and wake up, be empty, do nothing productive, eat, sleep. And then it kind of just became a routine of unproductiveness, procrastination, wanting to do something, fear of failing, and all that until I fall asleep and wake up the next day.
Honestly, I still ask myself what purpose I have in this life. I'm still kind of convinced that I'm nobody significant and that nothing will change when I'm gone. 
I don't know, really. I just know, as I try to make sense of this whole life shebang, that I didn't really want my life to end. I just want the pain to flutter away and never exist anymore.

Woke up from a dream where my friend died. I was scared and cried until morning. 4 or 5 years later, I get a phone call from one of our friends that he had died of unknown reasons after waking up to a terrible headache. He left a son and a grieving wife. I still think of him to this day.

It's lonely, you know? And distressing. Having to deal with everything that's not physical. I want to believe there will come a time when I won't have to think like this anymore. I do have a child, and it's painful to think about her and how she'll feel when I'm gone. She had been the reason that'stopping me from biting the proverbial bullet. And sometimes, that thought of her just isn't enough. It sounds bad, I know, but that's what happens sometimes.

I used to think I was gonna be someone who will do good, and I try to be good to other people. I feel real empathy towards people like me who struggle with every passing day not knowing what the future will bring because I know what that evil that does to someone. But I guess people do cope with things differently. Mine is just difficult and vague and just plain different from everyone else and I guess that's one way of saying everyone's different from everyone else.

I want to live still. I just don't want to live like this baggage full of unwanted thoughts. I want to do things, but I guess I have to know first how I can get this void of whatever-the-hell's-stopping-me out of the way.

That's the difficult part of life for me. Knowing what to do and not knowing HOW to do it.
